set R_LIBS=P:\R prg\R-2.11.1\library
set R_HOME=P:\R prg\R-2.11.1

However I'm getting the error msg that

"non-existent directory specified in --libpath=."

However the path assigned above is the correct path. Any ideas?

Regards,
M

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: deducer date time data
parts:
Bruce,

Deducer 0.4-3 added support for dates and times to the data viewer, so make sure you have the latest version of the package. When converting from strings, the viewer assumes that the format is year/month/day rather than the day/month/year of your data. So you will have to use the command line to get your variables into the right class.

There is a limitation on the size of data that the data viewer can handle. I hope to remove this limitation in a future release. Experimenting with my own system, the data viewer starts to choke up after 25 million cells ( I tried a set with 500,000 observations and 50 variables). If you work with large datasets, I recommend just keeping the data viewer closed.


Ian

messages.subject: Re: deducer date time data
parts:
Bruce,

So I've added better date and time conversion to the data viewer,
supporting a variety of formats. There is really no reason the user
should be limited to the 2010-10-10 format. This will be available in
the 0.4-4 release of deducer.

To do what you want, you do need to write a few lines of R code to
manipulate the Time variable into a numeric format. Perhaps I'll add a
string manipulation dialog at some point, but I don't see that
happening too soon.

ian

Mormoopids <- read.table("/Users/ianfellows/Downloads/Mormoopids.CSV",header=T,sep=",",quote="")
#open data dialog
Mormoopids[,3]<-as.Date(Mormoopids[,3], format= '%m/%d/%Y')
#Deducer 0.4-4 Data viewer type conversion

#hand written code to convert time into numeric
tmp <- strsplit(Mormoopids$Time,":")
Mormoopids$Hour <- sapply(tmp,function(x) as.numeric(x[1]) +
as.numeric(x[2])/60 )
#end hand written code

#plot builder
dev.new()
ggplot() +
geom_density(aes(x = Hour,colour = Species),data=Mormoopids) +
theme_bw()

parts:
Misha,

I'm glad you finally got it working. I don't know how you had JGR
installed, but not rJava. 99% of the time JGR can be run by just
double clicking on the jgr-1_62.exe launcher. 1% of the time, however,
the user's R set-up is imposible to know a priori, and they must
specify the paths themselves. I view this unacceptably complex.

The development version of JGR now has a new feature to mitigate this
problem. If you can run require(JGR) in R, you should be able to
launch JGR. The steps are as follows

1. Open R

2. Install development JGR by running
install.packages('JGR',,'http://www.rforge.net/')

3. run
library(JGR)
JGR()

note: If you are not running Windows R>=2.12.0 you will need to use
install.packages('JGR',,'http://www.rforge.net/', type="source") to
get the development version of JGR.

Given the vast array of possible set-ups, I'd appreciate it if anyone
with a custom set-up (i.e. double clicking on the launcher doesn't cut
it) could try this and let me know if there are any problems.

Best,
Ian
